title: A file may import the package it already lives in
why: acme/core/leaf.py spelling its neighbour absolutely, as acme.core.helper, is the same import as a relative one — and acme/core/__init__.py was already running before leaf.py began. Counting that init as a fresh dependency invents a cycle between a directory and itself, which is the false positive the ancestor rule has to not create.
unexpressible: neither rival has a file-granular cross-directory cycle law, so there is nothing to ask them: this case exists to pin our own law against over-firing, which is the risk any ancestor-aware resolver takes on.
